lina: Heads up  KPI panel showing a weird step change in webinar conversions at 07:30 UTC. Can someone confirm if this is real or tagging noise?
omar: Pulling dashboard now. Which cohort? the April launch list?
kevin: Yep April launch. Raw signups doubled for a 25-minute window. No paid spend scheduled.
ops-bot: Event: partner-send-214 executed 2026-04-14T07:28:03Z recipients=3,100 template=partner-april-v1 links_tracked=true
lina: That likely explains the lift but our dashboard split is odd: some records map to campaign `apr_launch` others to `april-launch-a`.
omar: UTM mismatch. Our trendlines treat them as separate campaigns so week-over-week baseline looks inflated.
kevin: Suggestion: add a derived column `campaign_canonical` in the ETL mapping both variants -> `apr_launch`. Do not overwrite raw utm fields.
metrics-bot: Action queued: add ETL mapping rule `canonicalize_apr_launch`. ETA 45m.
lina: For the KPI readout in 30m, show raw vs canonical counts plus a footnote: "partner send at 07:28 caused one-off lift; series normalized for trend".
omar: Also include MQL% for the spike vs 7-day baseline to test quality. If quality is lower, mark as low-confidence.
kevin: I'll update the slide: three small panels (traffic vs baseline, raw signups, canonical signups + MQL%).
ops-bot: Note: link template updated to include param `?src=partner_apr_v1` to reduce future mismatches.
lina: One follow-up: can we add an automated alert that flags sudden campaign alias splits? Saves manual scrub.
metrics-bot: Feature request logged: "auto-detect campaign alias spikes" assigned to metrics team.
omar: Thanks all. Quick 10-min sync at 08:50 to finalize slide.
lina: Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
